title: Document running a worktree's slicer from outside it
lead: AGENTS.md "Landing a slice" tells an agent to run `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer` inside the new worktree. An agent that must not change directory has no stated way to do that, and the editable `slicer` on `PATH` may belong to another checkout.
findings_note: AGENTS.md says to run PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer inside the worktree, which needs a cd; PYTHONPATH with --root worked from the main checkout while taking s174
boundary: **Not in this slice:** adding a `--worktree` flag or any code change to slicer; changing the worktree process itself; editing the global agent rules.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `--root` already points slicer at another checkout. With `PYTHONPATH` set to that worktree's `src`, the worktree's code runs against the worktree's `.slicer/` from any directory. The guide should say so, so an agent does not fall back to the wrong `slicer` or to a `cd`.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `AGENTS.md` ("Landing a slice")
- `docs/agents.md` if it repeats the worktree instruction
- `CHANGELOG.md` only if a user-facing doc changes

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. The guide shows the no-`cd` form: `PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src python3 -m slicer --root <worktree> ...`.
2. Run from the main checkout, that form's `start`, `check`, and `done` change the worktree's `.slicer/` and leave the main checkout's `git status` clean.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Add the no-`cd` form next to the existing worktree instruction. Keep the in-worktree form, and say that `--root` is how to reach the worktree without changing directory.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: `slicer check`, `git diff --check`, and the run in test 2 on a scratch worktree. No code changes, so the unit suite is unaffected.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, including the re-rendered roadmap.
